sections.hypothesis: Weeks that start while BTC (ETH) costs more on Coinbase than on Binance, relative to its recent normal, are followed by better returns than weeks that start while it costs less.
sections.rationale: Who pays: crypto trades on segmented exchanges, and US dollar buyers (retail and, since 2024, ETF and institutional flow) reach it mostly through Coinbase. When they buy harder than the rest of the world, Coinbase's price rises above Binance's until arbitrage closes the gap, which is slow and capital-limited. A premium is net demand arriving; the bet is that the flow persists into the next week. Outside evidence: Makarov and Schoar (2020, Journal of Financial Economics, 'Trading and arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets') show large, persistent price gaps between exchanges that move with order flow, and that arbitrage between them is limited (checked 2026-11-22). Traders watch the 'Coinbase premium' as a US demand gauge, which is commentary, not evidence. Not a rejected family: it reads where buying comes from, not a price pattern. Independence from the trend bet is the point (findings 16), so it is tested directly below.
sections.rules: kestrel signal-study coinbase-premium BTCUSDT ETHUSDT. Daily premium = Coinbase close (BTC-USD, ETH-USD) / (Binance close (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT) x Coinbase USDT-USD close) - 1, all daily candles closing 00:00 UTC, so it is known at the decision close; the USDT-USD term removes USDT's own drift from a dollar. The signal is on when the mean premium over the 7 days to the Sunday close is above its median over the 180 days before those 7. Span: from the first Sunday with 187 days of USDT-USD (Coinbase lists it from 2021-05-04) to 2025-10. Each Sunday's daily close (UTC) is a sample; outcome: the log return of the Binance coin to the next Sunday's close. Samples a week apart never overlap; BTC and ETH are pooled (they move together, so the effective sample is smaller than the count). Never the holdout. Run once. Reported beside it, deciding nothing: the same from 2018-01 without the USDT adjustment.
sections.falsification: PROCEED only if P(spread > 0) is at least 90% (bootstrap), the spread (mean week after 'on' minus mean week after 'off') beats one round trip of costs (about 22 bps), and the independence control holds. Otherwise KILL. A PROCEED leads to a strategy note on the full scorecard (BTC and ETH's holdout years are spent, so it would be judged forward on paper); a KILL ends it. Its overlap with the pursued strategies is reported beside the result, deciding nothing. The independence control, fixed here: the spread is also measured separately in weeks whose past week rose and weeks whose past week fell. PROCEED needs the spread positive in both halves as well; if it lives in only one, the signal is momentum (or dip-buying, a rejected family) under another name, and that is a KILL, said plainly.
sections.parameters: None to choose: 7 days, the 180-day median and the weekly step are fixed here.
sections.costs: A study: one look. Data: Coinbase Exchange's public candles (free, no key), Binance bars already stored. A gap in either is reported, never filled.
